Comments On 1/28/2015, Range Resources reported a release of diesel-based drilling mud from the Union 209 rig while drilling the 10H well (081-21298). The pressurized release was caused by a failed weld on the flow (mud return) line and caused drill mud to be sprayed approximately 300'. The majority of the spill was on containment but an unknown volume sprayed on nearby mountain laurel, trees, and snow off the well pad. On 1/29/2015, I inspected the site. The Union 209 was idle while repairs were being made to the flow line. The majority of the released diesel-based drilling mud was excavated from the woods off containment but impacted trees remain standing. We marked the furthest extent of the release with pink surveyors tape and the impacted trees with orange surveyors tape. A crew was onsite preparing to remove the remaining impacted material while previously excavated material (impacted) was stockpiled on containment. On 1/30/2015, all impacted vegetation and snow removed for disposal. Violations Cited on 1/29/2015 were resolved on 1/30/2015

Comments: On 10/15/2025, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the R.SMITH well pad in Carroll Township, Washington County.The following was observed during inspection:- The Act 9 sign was located at the access road entrance in accordance with 78a55 requirements. The Emergency Response Plan was on site (Photo 1).- The well site entrance and access road appeared to be stabilized with no accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues observed (Photo 2).-The well site and well pad slopes was exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues observed (Photo 3 and 4).-PCSM Basin appeared to be constructed to site plans and functioning properly (Photo 5).-The Department found a spill 5x5 ft in diameter in front of the production tank collection and secondary containment. The spill was not reported to the Department. I observed elevated conductivity fluid of 6.10 mS/cm, 5.76 mS/cm, 3.51 mS/cm and 3.23 mS/cm (Photo 6-12). I observed over range fluid within collection containment grate and within production tank secondary containment (Photo 13 and 14).-Production fluid tanks and GPUs were observed in secondary containment (Photo 6, 15-17). I observed fluid leaking from the 13H wheel valve (Photo 18-20)-A well tag was observed on the well head (Photo 21).Field Scout Conductivity probe was calibrated on 10/15/2025 before inspection was conducted. The operator was notified of the spill on 10/15/2025.Violations are being issued for a spill found by the Department: 78a54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), 78a.66(b)(2).

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 3/20/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8180038
Permit API: 065-25577
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/20/2024
Comments: This site located east off Route 1830 in a forested area at the end of a road that accesses two Diversified wells. Well set-up for production with a meter, separator and one tank in secondary containment. Will Warfel notified the Department of a release of approximately 13 barrels from a brine tank as a result of a porcupine chewing a 2" plastic plug at the bottom of the tank located in secondary containment. The release of brine from the tank partially filled the secondary containment then seeped under the secondary containment and surfaced 10-15' south of the embankment and pooled on the surface. There was no evidence that the brine release moved off site. No equipment on site, all contaminated dirt in, around and including the secondary containment embankment has been removed from site. The excavated area has been covered by plastic until sampling is completed and restoration completed. Moody Associates Inc. will complete required sampling and Act 2 report for clean-up.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/12/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/12/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8284380
Permit API: 123-46784
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/12/2026
Comments: Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) reported a release of produced fluids at TMP's Brown Hill Road tank battery. The tank battery consists of five 210 bbl stock tanks (# 1053, 1054, 1055, 1056, 1057), a separator, gas meter, burner, and buried brine tank. The Brown Hill Church Lease, Lyszaz Lease, and R Brown Lease are plumbed to this tank battery.It was reported that lightning from recent thunderstorms must have struck the tanks, ignited combustible contents, and caused an explosion that expanded and ruptured four out of the five tanks. The released fluid flowed through the ruptures and into the secondary containment area. It was reported that at the time of the release, the stock tanks were mostly empty but did contain some sludge from prior storage of produced fluids.Brian Bennett of TMP was onsite at the time of this inspection to discuss cleanup expectations with Evan Bruce (WQS) and I (Mathew Haemer - WQS). Brian estimated that the volume of the released fluids was approximately 4 bbl. Brian explained that he had been working on mixing sawdust with the sludge that had filled the containment area and had begun to remove the saturated sawdust to temporary storage in barrels staged inside the secondary containment area.At the time of this inspection, the buried brine tank was nearly empty. The majority of the release pooled around the buried brine tank. Brine was not reported to be a suspected component of this release. However, elevated SPC readings were observed both in the sawdust/sludge mixture (5,350 uS/cm) and in the soils of the secondary containment area's western end (8,900 uS/cm).Two groundhog holes were observed in the northwest corner of the secondary containment area. Elevated SPC readings (4,140/12,250 uS/cm) were observed in the soil inside of the groundhog holes. This indicates that at one point in time, brine discharged into the secondary containment area rose to a level sufficient to spill over into the holes, and from that point migrate outside of containment. A storage yard has been constructed downslope of the tank battery. HDPE pipe is scattered at one end, and spare pump jacks at the other. Coincidentally, the soil is visibly wet beneath the area where the HDPE pipe is scattered. Elevated SPC of soils (1,468 uS/cm) was observed where the pipe is scattered. The disturbed earth above the pipe and pump jacks also had elevated SPC readings (1,346 uS/cm). A violation for failure to construct and maintain a method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112 is being cited due to the evidence that brine was able to migrate through the secondary containment wall via the groundhog holes and/or through permeating the earthen containment.The quantity of the release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold set forth in the Department's spill policy, therefore either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required. It is requested that the source and extent of the release be identified.

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Comments: On November 8, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection for a reported spill at the Inflection Energy TLC Pad. The DEP received a phone call from Inflection Energy Zac Subra on November 6, 2021 about a release of production fluid during a pressure test. The DEP met with Inflection Energy Joe Zoka. During a pressure test for the preparation of flowback of the recently drilled wells, a valve was left open. The open valve spilled about 28 gallons of brine fluid to the pad surface. The impacted area was excavated immediately. Inflection scraped about 3 inches of a 15 ft. by 10 ft. area. The impacted soil was then loaded into a covered container to be hauled to the landfill. The containment around the flowback equipment appears to be in good condition. Inflection is planning to begin flowback process on Tuesday. Violations of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), ¿78a.56(a), and SWMA 301 are noted but have been immediately corrected. Outstanding violations remain from Inspection Report 3257683.

Comments: On May 27, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039, where violations were issued for broken and corroded piping and a release from broken and corroded piping.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4106039, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department attempted to contact the Operator by calling the number posted on the well tag, however, the number was not in service, therefore violations are being issued at this time for failure to have updated and accurate information posted on the well posting.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank under/adjacent to the corroded pipes. Although, these soil conductivity readings (0.0328 mS, 0.0899 mS, and 0.0244 mS) are not elevated, it does not visual appear that the release that previously occurred has yet to be remediated as vegetation in this area appears to be distressed and the gravel in this area is stained. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment, the Department recommends any equipment not in use be removed from the well site. Violations are being issued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping is to remain outstanding at this time and new violations are being issued at this time for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.

Comments: On May 27, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039, where violations were issued for broken and corroded piping and a release from broken and corroded piping.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4106039, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it. Comments: The Department, Frank Hoehle, DEP O&G WQS and I arrived at the site at 11:39 to conduct a follow up inspection in reference to a production fluid spill that occurred at the site on 1-6-19. The weather conditions are cloudy skies, breezy, with rainfall approaching, and a temperature of 35 degrees Fahrenheit. For additional details pertaining to the production fluid spill, refer to the Department's 1-6-19, 1-9-19, and 1-17-19 inspection reports, Inspection ID#'s 2831500, 2832214, 2832221. We met with Murray Kush, site company man, completions consultant of Repsol, and Dave Coxhead, Site Safety Man, of REM Security. Deep Well Services Rig # 2 is in the process of drilling out hydraulic fracturing plugs. Mr. Kush informed the Department the following. "The rig is drilling out frac plugs on the 3H well. A total of 22 plugs will be drilled out. We are the 20th plug. The 1H is done. Frac plugs will be drilled out on the 7H next. The working tanks and gas buster tanks near the pad entrance contain fluid from the 3H plug drill outs. Brine was used on the 1H well to drill out the plugs. Fresh water is used to drill out the plugs on the 3H well. Trucks are removing water from 1H plug drill outs, out of the offloading station near the production equipment. Containment is the same since the frac. We added containment under the rig. Gel is used to drill out plug parts." In addition to conducting a follow-up inspection at the site, the Department conducted a review of sample results for a water sample collected at the site on 1-9-19. The PADEP Bureau of Laboratories in Harrisburg, PA forwarded the results to the Department on 2-6-19. On 1-9-19, the Department collected a groundwater sample from the swale at the base of the Caprio Pad where the water exhibited elevated levels conductivity on 1-8-18. The Department identified this water sample as Caprio Pad SW-1. Upon review of the Department's groundwater sample results, it was noted that the sample results had elevated concentrations of barium, lithium, manganese, strontium, aluminum, chloride, and iron. Barium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential Medium Specific Concentration (MSC) for groundwater of 2,000 micrograms per liter (ug/l) with a concentration of 50,600 ug/l. Lithium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 83 ug/l for Residential, Used Aquifers and for Non-residential, Used Aquifers of 230 ug/l with a concentration of 1,270 ug/l. Manganese was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 300 ug/l with a concentration of 8,000 ug/l. Strontium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 4,000 ug/l with a concentration of 38,900 ug/l. Aluminum was detected above the Act 2, Secondary Maximum Contaminant Level (SMCL) of 200 ug/l with a concentration of 41,400 ug/l. Chloride was detected above the Act 2, SMCL of 250,000 ug/l with a concentration of 946,000 ug/l. Iron was detected above the Act 2, SMCL of 300 ug/l with a concentration of 34,400 ug/l. Bromide was detected at a concentration of 7,307.28 ug/l. Calcium was detected at a concentration of 252,000 ug/l. Sodium was detected at a concentration of 389,000 ug/l. Specific See the attached sample results. During the inspection, I utilized a Hanna Groline Soil Test HI 98331 meter, and an Oakton PCTS 50 meter to record specific conductance (conductivity) in water in the sump in the infiltration basin at the toe of fill slope, and in water and damp soil west and slightly up-gradient of the sump, where groundwater seeped to the fill slope. Conductivity readings were in the range of (170-240) microsiemens/cm in the sump, and (700-800) microsiemens/cm in water west of the sump, and (150-200) microsiemens/cm in wet soil west of the sump. See photos. The Department left the site at 12:43.

On 6/25/2021, the Operator reported that more than 5 gallons of produced water was spilled to the well pad from a Gas Production Unit dump line. At the time of inspection, SPSI and Moody and Associates were in the process of remediating the impacted material and flushing the well pad drains. The Moody and Associates representative Jona Stosky indicated that the operator would be utilizing Act 2 clean up standards for brine. Ms. Stosky indicated that approximately 90 yards of impacted material has been removed from the well pad and placed in roll off disposal boxes. Ms. Stosky indicated that additional material may need to be removed to remediate the well pad. I observed staining on the dump line associated with the GPU labeled as the 10H. The remediation crew was flushing and or washing the well pad drain and the area under the 10H GPU unit with fresh water to flush out the production fluid. On 6/29/2021, I spoke with EQT representative David Crayne., Mr. Crayne indicated that approximately 42 gallons of production fluid was released. The spill appeared to be contained on the well pad. Violations are being issued in relation to the release of a regulated material.

Unconventional: No

Comments: On March 19 2025 the Department conducted an inspection of the RWS Development 001 OG Well in regards to an incident reported to the Department of an explosion and fire at the well site on 3/19/2025 at 1:00 pm. Present during the inspection were several representatives from the Manor Volunteer Fire Department, Westmoreland City Fire Department, Jay Niehenke (Kriebel), Ronald Seich (Kriebel) Ben Dickun (Kriebel) and Charles Reaggle (DEP).-This is inspection 1 of a 2 part inspection-The findings are as follows:Upon the Department's arrival to the well site, no active fire was observed. The Department spoke to fire department representative Brian Williams who stated they used approximately 3200 gallons of municipal water from their firetruck as well as Dawn Dish Soap at a 0.6% per gallon concentration to extinguish the fire on site. While onsite, the SDS sheet for Dawn Dish Soap used was sent to the Department electronically by the Fire Department Representative Brian Williams. According to the SDS sheet, "Ecotoxicity- The product is not expected to be hazardous to the environment."Upon inspection of the production equipment, the Department observed damage to the equipment including a hole in the production tank as a result of the incident. Upon inspection of the hole in the production tank, the Department observed a small intermittent trickle of fluid from the production tank hole, down the side of the tank to the ground. A soil conductivity reading was taken directly under the hole in the tank with a reading of OR (over detectable range, >20.0 mS). The Department inquired what the most recent tank level was prior to the incident. Mr. Dickun stated that it was believed to be approximately 2 feet 6 inches from the bottom, however the date and exact measurement was unknown as that information is stored on a computer and was unable to be accessed at the time of the inspection. The Department took a measurement of the of the hole in the tank, which appeared level with the fluid level and obtained a measurement of approximately 2 feet 10.5 inches. While onsite, a truck arrived and began emptying the fluid from the production tank.The Department then assessed the well site to determine impacts resulting from any releases on the site as a result of the explosion/ fire and resulting measures taken to extinguish it. The Department observed a ditch/channel approximately 15 feet behind the well. The ditch appeared to run approximately 180 feet where it terminates just before a stream. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. The Department also observed absorbent pads in the ditch that were reportedly placed placed by the Fire Department. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of OR, 6.28mS, 5.75mS, and 5.25mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. Conductivity readings were taken in this area of the ditch with readings of 0.42mS, 0.34mS, and 0.42mS.The Department then took conductivity readings of the water in the stream. A conductivity reading was taken upstream of where the ditch appears to terminate with a reading of 0.65mS. There appeared to be a large amount of debris and trash in the stream and on the stream bank upstream where this conductivity reading was taken. A conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.90mS. Comments: On March 19 2025 the Department conducted an inspection of the RWS Development 001 OG Well in regards to an incident reported to the Department of an explosion and fire at the well site on 3/19/2025 at 1:00 pm. Present during the inspection were several representatives from the Manor Volunteer Fire Department, Westmoreland City Fire Department, Jay Niehenke (Kriebel), Ronald Seich (Kriebel) Ben Dickun (Kriebel) and Charles Reaggle (DEP).-This is inspection 1 of a 2 part inspection-The findings are as follows:Upon the Department's arrival to the well site, no active fire was observed. The Department spoke to fire department representative Brian Williams who stated they used approximately 3200 gallons of municipal water from their firetruck as well as Dawn Dish Soap at a 0.6% per gallon concentration to extinguish the fire on site. While onsite, the SDS sheet for Dawn Dish Soap used was sent to the Department electronically by the Fire Department Representative Brian Williams. According to the SDS sheet, "Ecotoxicity- The product is not expected to be hazardous to the environment."Upon inspection of the production equipment, the Department observed damage to the equipment including a hole in the production tank as a result of the incident. Upon inspection of the hole in the production tank, the Department observed a small intermittent trickle of fluid from the production tank hole, down the side of the tank to the ground. A soil conductivity reading was taken directly under the hole in the tank with a reading of OR (over detectable range, >20.0 mS). The Department inquired what the most recent tank level was prior to the incident. Mr. Dickun stated that it was believed to be approximately 2 feet 6 inches from the bottom, however the date and exact measurement was unknown as that information is stored on a computer and was unable to be accessed at the time of the inspection. The Department took a measurement of the of the hole in the tank, which appeared level with the fluid level and obtained a measurement of approximately 2 feet 10.5 inches. While onsite, a truck arrived and began emptying the fluid from the production tank.The Department then assessed the well site to determine impacts resulting from any releases on the site as a result of the explosion/ fire and resulting measures taken to extinguish it. The Department observed a ditch/channel approximately 15 feet behind the well. The ditch appeared to run approximately 180 feet where it terminates just before a stream. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. The Department also observed absorbent pads in the ditch that were reportedly placed placed by the Fire Department. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of OR, 6.28mS, 5.75mS, and 5.25mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. Conductivity readings were taken in this area of the ditch with readings of 0.42mS, 0.34mS, and 0.42mS.The Department then took conductivity readings of the water in the stream. A conductivity reading was taken upstream of where the ditch appears to terminate with a reading of 0.65mS. There appeared to be a large amount of debris and trash in the stream and on the stream bank upstream where this conductivity reading was taken. A conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.90mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 8/09/2022
Comments: This conventional well has recently been produced with a pump jack, there was no activity on this location or throughout the Cole Creek lease during this inspection.A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl steel stock tank and a poly brine/production water tank is located approximately 150 feet to the south of this well. These tanks are contained by an earthen dyking which has been lined and partially filled with gravel. Holes have formed throughout the exposed portion of the liner along the upper edge of the containment wall.Fluid was trickling out of the containment drain pipe into the roadside ditch upon my arrival at the tank battery. There was no supervision of this discharge and the drain is not equipped with a valve. A shower drain cover was fitted onto the inlet of this drain. The specific conductivity (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment exceeded the upper threshold of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Pooled fluid in the ditch was also greater than 20,000 uS/cm. Deer tracks are abundant around the pooled fluid in the roadside ditch. This evidence suggests that the fluid being discharged from the containment drain is production water/brine. An SAC 941 sample was collected from the fluid discharging from the drain. The fluid in the roadside ditch flowed through a cross culvert and into a forested area. Poor road conditions have allowed stormwater to run off of the road surface above this culvert, which allowed the released fluid to migrate further into the forested area. Elevated SPC of pooled water and soil (along with stressed vegetation) was observed in various pathways across the forest floor west of the tank battery for approximately 200 feet downslope of the tank battery. The most downward extent of the apparent impacted soil (near a property boundary/corner marker) is approaching a channel (currently dry) that develops into an unnamed tributary of Cole Creek.After this inspection, I spoke with Justin Hansen of Bull Run to discuss the aforementioned issues along with concerns regarding the roads, site identification and actions necessary to consider this well site restored. In order to consider utilizing the containment drain, the fluid that is currently pooled inside of the containment will need to be removed along with the saturated gravel. Prior to any future discharges from the drain, the water should be tested as per the regulations to ensure it meets the criteria to be released under sufficient supervision.Future inspections will be conducted to review the current state of affairs with Bull Run personnel and evaluate remediation measures outside of the containment as they take place.

I arrived on site with Brady Johnson (DEP) and we met Brett Bunker (Hilcorp Energy). He filled us in on the clean up details. Basically, they have moved the compressor and excavated most of the impacted material and are just dealing with some "hot spot" areas. The spill hit hard pan under the gravel and confined the oil to mainly only traveling 8" to 12" vertically. The impacted material was in 4 roll off containers and they will have more as the contractor (ACV Enviro) is continuing to remove some more contaminated material. Brett feels the clean up work should be done by the end of today.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/03/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/03/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8227912
Permit API: 123-47902
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/03/2025
Comments: The R H Stevenson Lease 4 conventional well is the nearest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the R H Stevenson lease. The tank battery is situated within earthen containment and consists of an upper level containing two stock tanks, and a lower level containing two polyurethane tanks. The stock tanks are plumbed into PVC piping that extends along the rear of the upper level of the earthen containment until terminating into the first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level. The first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level is also equipped with additional PVC piping apparently for the purpose of either removing or depositing fluids into the tank in the lower level of containment. At the time of this inspection, standing pools of fluid present in the upper level of the containment were found to have specific conductance measuring 5,980 microSiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). It was observed that straw had been laid down beneath the PVC piping in the upper level of containment. Where the straw cover ends, fluid was found to be actively flowing from the upper level of containment to the lower level. No fluid was observed to be flowing through the PVC piping connecting the stock tanks to the polyurethane tank during the time of this inspection. Neither polyurethane stock tank was found to have a noticeable volume of fluids contained within them at the time of this inspection. Some accumulation of fluids and crude oil could be observed around the base of the polyurethane tanks in the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection. The flow of fluids from the upper level to the lower level of containment was not found to be accumulating nor increasing the accumulated volume of fluids and crude oil present at the bottom of the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection.Approximately 40 feet south of the lower level tank battery containment area, crude oil and production fluids emerged on the soil surface. This flow of fluids continues west and is visually impacted by crude oil for approximately 180 feet. From there, soils and standing fluid with elevated specific conductance continue for approximately 75 feet before reaching a culvert. A pool of fluid at the entrance of the culvert was found to have specific conductance measuring 6,820 uS/cm.From the culvert, the fluid continues southwest in the natural swale for approximately 115 feet before reaching a point at which the swale transitions to an unnamed tributary (UNT) stream of Jackson Run, with defined bed and banks. At this point, waters in the UNT had specific conductance measuring 5,510 uS/cm. Specific conductance of 2,750 uS/cm was observed in the waters of the UNT in the remaining approximately 180 foot stretch, at which point there is a confluence with a second UNT of Jackson Run. Immediately before the confluence, waters in the impacted stream with specific conductance of 1,923 uS/cm were observed. Approximately two feet downstream of the confluence at a point with coordinates 41.95555, -79.29740 was the apparent end of impact to the UNTs of Jackson Run, where waters in the stream had a measured specific conductance of 42.6 uS/cm.At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the well.On 04/04/25 I called and spoke with William Cenk and Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. Mr. Cenk and Mr. Miller agreed to meet with Department officials onsite next week. A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, corrosion, and possible failures. As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. All valves were open and the well is currently equipped for production. 2 check valves were in place on the production lines and were oriented correctly. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation. NO methane was detected in the slam bar holes utilizing a MSA ALTAIR 5X meter which was calibrated on 07/17/2023. Pressures observed at the time of inspection were: 4.2psi on the 6-5/8"x2" annulus and 4psi on the inside of the 2" tubing. This well was labeled with an incorrect well API#, this issue was brought to the attention of the operator and promptly fixed. Further inspections of this well may be warranted to determine the root cause of the complaint.

Comments: Routine field inspection performed in afternoon with cool, partly cloudy with sunny weather conditions and 55 degrees. Last inspection performed on 5/14/02, more than 20 years ago. Wellhead is located in field between Agriculture fields planted with corn, recently harvested ~275' SW of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). At the wellhead surface casing valve is open, lower right side production tubular valve open to port and domestic house gas meter run, valve to port is closed, valve to drip and meter is open, lower production tubular left side valve is cracked open, upper production tubular is plumbed with no valve unions, and the production tubular plumbed on left side (opposite meter) of head to sales/surface equipment has open valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photo #2). Meter reading and open valve after meter (photo #3). Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead (photo #4). Some trace to occasionally fair corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility and one 50 bbl poly tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #5). Valve open on main tubular feeding separator with open valves to and from separator (photo #6). A 31-day production chart is present with recordings and dated 10/4/22 (photo #7). Well posting signage partially affixed to cabinet jacket door of production recording apparatus with all information about well and current Operator present, except Operator address information (photo #8). Trace to occasionally fair corrosion on ground production unit equipment. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). Operator contact address information is missing from posting and needs added. Posting needs to be permanently affixed to facility, at present the upper left side of posting has lost adhesive and has folded over itself resulting in an unreadable posting (photos #5 background and #8). The Operator submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well stating 80 psig. The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 378.72 MCF recorded over 365 days. Wellhead field verified and GPS coordinates of well updated with this inspection showed a minimal distance offset of ~35 ft between coordinates (photo #9). This is an active, producing well with a domestic house gas meter at wellhead.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of a routine inspection. The well is currently awaiting a service rig, per the operator, and has not been recently pumped. It appears as though a leak occurred on this site sometime in the past year, and it was covered with absorbent peat and then left. The spill was not reported to DEP. The quantity of oil spilled is unknown, but appears to be greater than 5 gallons and less than one barrel. Oil stained soil with absorbent peat is noted in an L shape approximately 10 feet wide and 30 feet long that extends to the edge of the location. Absorbent peat is noted closer to the edge of the site, primarily. A small UNT of Briggs Run begins at the edge of the site. One oil soaked pad was noted in this ditch lone, although no oil was noted in the ditch at this time. The operator was contacted and they arrived on site to begin assessment and cleanup on 8/25. Per the operator, the spill occurred over this past winter and the well pumper covered the spill with peat sorb, which then settled as it was not cleaned up as the winter went on. Spring melt allowed the material to run to the edge of the site. Per the operator, the employee is no longer with the company. Cleanup should be completed in the next few days. Followup inspection will be performed at that time.The operator was also asked about the steep and rutted access roads on this lease and said that they have recently acquired a new bulldozer and intend to grade and fix lease roads soon.

Comments: The operator called the Department to report a spill that was found the morning of 7/31/2020. Per the operator, a leak of brine occurred from a poly tank or the line leading from the separator to the tank and leaked into containment. It then ran around a freshwater drain pipe that was placed in at construction.The well is an open flowing well that appears to in production, with the valves opened. The well is plumbed to a gas separator and a 50 barrel poly tank within containment. Some stained soil is apparent between the separator and the containment, with elevated conductivity >1mS noted using a Soil EC meter probe. Vegetation within the containment is distressed or dead, indicating brine discharge. Down slope from the containment, vegetation has been killed in a band consistent with discharge from or around the freshwater drain. Conductivity measured ~11 mS near the drain and diminished down slope, with the final reading over 1 mS noted approximately 100 feet from the tank, in a scour location that was likely from a stormwater event. The total volume of brine leaked is likely close to the Operator's estimate of 30-35 gallons, with approximately 5-10 gallons being outside containment.The operator was called back. They said that they would have a contractor on site to dig up impacted soil early next week. Followup inspection will be dome then.

The total volume of brine leaked is likely close to the Operator's estimate of 30-35 gallons, with approximately 5-10 gallons being outside containment.The operator was called back. They said that they would have a contractor on site to dig up impacted soil early next week. Followup inspection will be dome then.

Comments: On February 3 2023, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill release reported by the Operator on 2/2/2023 for the Cummins 1 OG Well. Accompanying in today's inspection was Ron Truitt (Penneco Represenative). The findings were as follows:Per Ron Truitt, produced water was released due to the overflowing of the right production tank. The nipple (where the two tanks connect)at the top of the production tank was frozen and did not allow back flow from one tank to another. The back flow not being able to flow from one tank to another caused the right tank to overflow. Per Ron Truitt, it was estimated that approximately 1 barrel of produced water was released. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the affected area in accordance with the spill policy for releases greater than 42 gallons.At the time of the inspection, clean up was being conducted. The production tanks were being emptied. Impacted area was being excavated. The Department requests that the Operator submit waste manifests once available. The Department will conduct a follow up inspection to verify that all impacted material has been removed. Based on today's inspection violations are being issued.

Comments: This inspection focuses on multiple discharges from various tanks that are located in the proximity of this well. An approximate 210 bbl portable steel stock tank is actively discharging crude oil from a corroded part of the tank. The fluid is currently discharging at a minimal rate and likely only occurs during hot, sunny conditions which liquifies the residual paraffin at the bottom of the tank. At this time, there is approximately 10 gallons of free crude near the tank and a 5' x 10' area of oil soaked ground downslope of the discharge point. Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Beaver Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/13/2021
Comments: This well was drilled in an agricultural area off of Shields Road in March 1996. A voicemail was left by Lane Simpson of Snyder Bros at 9:59 on 9/13/2021 to inform the Department of a spill at this site. The landowner struck the 100 bbl fiberglass brine tank with a haybine on Saturday evening, 9/11/2021. At that time, the landowner did not believe any serious damage occurred. On the morning of 9/12/2021, the landowner observed a large area of brine and soap suds downslope from the tank. This incident was reported to Snyder Bros on Monday morning (9/13). The well tender's estimate of lost production fluid was 15-20 bbl. At the time of inspection, the remaining production fluid had been drained from the brine tank, but work had not yet started on removing the contaminated soil. Lane Simpson was on-site awaiting the arrival of two rolloff containers. Remediation of the spill will begin as soon as equipment arrives on site. The tank appears to have been damaged beyond repair and should be replaced. The access will also likely require maintenance at the conclusion of remediation activities. Because the estimated spill volume is greater than 1 bbl, an Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process should be followed.
